entities.summary: Nerida Gaye Wilson is an invertebrate marine molecular biologist at the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation who has interests in diversity, systematics, phylogeny, phylogeography and behavior. Wilson has been instrumental in demonstrating the level of marine cryptic species complexes in Antarctic waters, testing the circumpolar distribution paradigm with molecular data, and using interdisciplinary approaches to show how Antarctic diversity may have been generated. Her work with NOAA on Antarctic Marine Living Resources has been used to regulate exploratory benthic fisheries.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Wilson's work has significantly advanced our understanding of Antarctic biodiversity and its potential origins, informing conservation efforts and fisheries management. Her research has also highlighted the need for interdisciplinary approaches to studying complex ecosystems.
